corpus_basis: Additional online Sanskrit-transcription witnesses to the already inventoried five-book study, primarily cross-checking the uploaded Portuguese BPHS and B41 Jataka interpretations.
reason_no_count_increase: Witnesses/collations and adjacent verse readings have not yet been globally de-duplicated against B01–B42; recollation is not counted as independent new book rules.

witnesses.textual_result: Residence away from home is one of the domains judged from the tenth house, alongside livelihood, honor, father and debts.
With the sixth lord in the second: living outside one's own locality, happiness, public speaking and work engagement are asserted; international border-crossing is not specified.
With the sixth lord in the tenth: a favorable experience in a foreign place, alongside public recognition, speech and father-related qualification; no citizenship claim.
With the eleventh lord in the sixth: living away from one's place appears with unfavorable health/hostility indicators, not with inevitable successful migration.
The preceding house-lord statements require strength/weakness judgment, so literal unqualified yes/no rules omit an explicit source limitation.
witnesses.editorial_notice: VedicPupil displays only the latter hemistich; the siva.sh witness contains both.

witnesses.textual_result: For two-sign planetary lords, effects for both lordships are to be considered; equal opposing effects cancel, according to the verse.
Distinct results are said to occur together; strong/medium-strength planets yield full/half effects according to traditional source language; these are not calibrated outcome probabilities.
The continuation assigns a quarter effect to low-strength planets; this is a historical interpretive scale, not measured probability.
In the Moon major period's Venus subperiod, favorable Venus placement relative to the main-period lord is associated with property/land growth and gain.
An adverse Venus subperiod configuration describes difficulties associated with foreign residence; Sanskrit alone does not establish deportation, despite that word in the displayed English rendering.

editorial_restrictions: Online Sanskrit transcriptions are not an independently established critical manuscript edition.
Two websites that appear to transmit the same text are not two historical confirmations.
Preserve B42 Portuguese source records and B41 Jataka source readings unchanged.
No copied copyrighted PDF/text or biography-based calibration.
Source arithmetic/verbal effect fractions are not probability scores.
